claim: Bobcats exhibited primarily nocturnal activity wherever they were present
design: One-sample proportion vs 50% (solar night = half the circle), clustered by site
effect_size_CI: 67.3% of detections nocturnal (naive 95% CI 52.5-80.1); site-level mean 55.8% (95% CI 30.3-82.7); 69.1% across the 7 sites with n>=5

claim: Domestic cats were primarily nocturnal at sites where no bobcats were detected
design: One-sample proportion vs 50%, clustered by site

claim: Diel activity of bobcats and domestic cats was similar where only one species occurred
design: Two-sample circular, but species is perfectly confounded with site set
test_indicated: Watson's U2 is the right family; the contrast is not identifiable, and an absence claim needs an equivalence margin
recomputed_p: U2=0.0753 (exact reproduction), asymptotic p=0.4469; 30-min filtered U2=0.0855, p=0.3674

claim: High overlap between diel activity patterns at solo sites, Dhat = 0.852
design: Point estimate of a coefficient of overlap (not a test)
test_indicated: Dhat1 with a bootstrap interval (the deposited script computes one)
effect_size_CI: Dhat1=0.8525 reproduced exactly; smoothed bootstrap 95% CI 0.726-0.895; site-clustered 95% CI 0.574-0.856; Dhat4=0.842

claim: Domestic cat diel activity differed significantly from bobcat activity where the two co-occurred
design: Two-sample circular, both species at the same 7 sites
n_defensible: 7 sites; 28 vs 91 detections after a 30-min independence filter
test_indicated: Watson's U2 on independence-filtered detections with a site-stratified permutation null
recomputed_p: U2=0.1893 (exact reproduction), asymptotic p=0.0476; 30-min filtered U2=0.1500, p=0.1036; site-stratified permutation p=0.0720; both corrections p=0.1162
effect_size_CI: Dhat1=0.6465 (site-clustered 95% CI 0.494-0.759); no effect size reported in the paper

claim: Activity patterns overlapped much less where the species co-occurred (Dhat 0.647 vs 0.852)
design: Difference between two overlap coefficients estimated on disjoint site sets
test_used: none - visual contrast of two point estimates
test_indicated: Bootstrap interval on the difference, resampled at the site level
effect_size_CI: difference 0.206; detection-level bootstrap 95% CI -0.004 to 0.312; site-clustered 95% CI -0.088 to 0.310

claim: Where bobcats were present domestic cats shifted to more daytime activity (51% vs 85% nocturnal)
design: Between-site-group comparison of the same species
n_defensible: 19 vs 7 sites (3 shared sites with n>=5)
test_indicated: Watson's U2 or a proportion contrast with a site-level null
recomputed_p: Watson's U2=1.281, detection-level p=2.1e-11; site-level permutation p=0.0585; %night site-permutation (detection-weighted) p=0.0034; site as unit (n>=5, 17 vs 3) p=0.0881
effect_size_CI: 34.0 pct-pt detection-level difference; 24.5 pct-pt site-level difference, bootstrap 95% CI 11.8-36.3

claim: Bobcats were detected more frequently in areas with <=65% developed land, domestic cats with >=65%
design: Two-group comparison of a site-level covariate
test_indicated: Site-level two-group test on the continuous covariate, no post hoc cutpoint
recomputed_p: not recomputable - per-site land cover is not in the deposit
effect_size_CI: none reported; the 65% cutpoint equals the shared-site group mean

claim: Land cover composition differed among the three site groups (50+/-19%, 82+/-14%, 65+/-16% developed)
test_indicated: none required for a descriptive statement
recomputed_p: not recomputable - per-site land cover is not in the deposit
effect_size_CI: means +/- 1 s.d. as reported; not verifiable

claim: Temporal and spatial niche partitioning appear to facilitate predator coexistence
design: Observational, cross-sectional, no randomisation or within-site contrast
test_indicated: No design here can separate species interaction from the urban gradient
effect_size_CI: site type is confounded with developed-land cover (50% vs 82% vs 65%) and distance from downtown
